what: ask 5's population half, second clean wave. Turn-125 autosave timeline (the draw-1 branch), eleven cities struck by a centred WMD_THERMONUCLEAR_DEVICE, each from its OWN bomber, none of their populations touched, polled 310 times to stability. AKKAD was out of bomber range and never fired - it is the untouched control. The blast content of every target was measured BEFORE the strike, so the loss can be fitted against something other than population.

note: out of bomber range, never fired - the untouched control, confirming nothing global moved population during the wave

reads: the two independent waves AGREE on every city they share, across a reload and across two different timelines: OTSU 4->4, NAPATA 5->2 and 5->3, NAN_MADOL 7->7, MONTROSE 8->1, NGAZARGAMU 10->10, MUSCAT 12->11, OKAYAMA 13->6. The population outcome is deterministic and reproducible, not rolled.

a nuke DESTROYS NO DISTRICT AND NO BUILDING. districtsInBlast, districtsTotal and buildingsTotal are identical before and after for all eleven struck cities. It pillages them (every district in the radius reads IsPillaged true) and leaves them standing. Only INCOMPLETE districts are removed, and that was measured on the capture path, not here.

the loss tracks the number of the city's COMPLETE DISTRICTS inside the blast radius, not its population. <=2 districts in the blast -> 0 or 1 population lost (OTSU 1 district loss 0; NAN_MADOL, NGAZARGAMU, MUSCAT 2 districts, losses 0, 0, 1 from populations 7, 10 and 12). >=3 districts -> the city is gutted, usually to population 1 (OSAKA, MONTROSE, NAGOYA, MEROE, DUNDEE all end at 1). A pop-12 city-state with two districts lost ONE citizen while a pop-12 major with four districts was reduced to one.

major-vs-minor is CONFOUNDED with the district count in this sample: all three city-states happened to have exactly 2 districts in the blast, and the only major with fewer than 3 (OTSU, 1 district) also lost nothing. The next run must break the tie - strike a city-state with 3+ districts, or a major with exactly 2 - before the rule can be written as 'districts' rather than 'city-states are nearly immune'.

two majors reproducibly do NOT go to 1: OKAYAMA (9 districts in the blast, 13 -> 6, in BOTH waves) and NAPATA (4 districts, 5 -> 3 and 5 -> 2). More districts did not mean more loss - OKAYAMA has the most districts of any target and kept the most people of any gutted major. Whatever sets the floor is still unmeasured.
